main_body: desert mud-brick building with flat rooftop terrace and front facade
top_band: light tan rooftop terrace with parapet walls, rug, and hatch from row 0 to row 31
evidence: Rows 0-31 show a full foreshortened horizontal rooftop terrace (with parapet lip, rug, and ladder hatch) in lighter tan tones. Rows 28-31 mark the front parapet edge and highlight, rows 32-33 form a dark overhang/eave shadow, and rows 34-63 show the darker terracotta front wall with recessed beam ends, inset arched doorway, and recessed window.

style.evidence: The mud-brick building uses warm brown/terracotta material outlines rather than black, and has 5-6 value steps across the roof sand/plaster and brick wall. The roof and wall carry plaster speckle, exposed brick patches, beam holes, a lattice window, and a detailed door, though the overall micro-contrast and per-tile density are slightly simpler than the tiled roofs and stone walls of the Beodeul references.
